To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
model-based dispatch strategies can be applied to lithium-ion batteries to reduce the cost of secondary reserve provision.
(1) model-based optimization of LiB dispatch strategies can significantly reduce costs, and (2) the benefit of LiB operation is strongly dependent on the specific market design.
the cost savings from using LiB for secondary reserve can be significantly increased by using cost-minimizing model-based dispatch strategies, and that these cost savings are substantial.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
    - What is the benefit of using LiB for secondary reserve provision?
a novel application of LiB in the German power system.

a) the development of an electro-thermal battery model that can be used to estimate state-dependent usage cost and b) the application of model-based optimization techniques for the dispatch of LiB to secondary reserve markets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of model-based dispatch strategies is beneficial for both the battery operator and the system operator.
a cost minimizing strategy is superior to a maximum usage strategy.
the cost savings from model-based optimization strategies are significant, but that the exact amount is highly dependent on the specific application scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed dispatch strategies are able to reduce the avoided cost of reserve by about 50% in a real-life market environment.
model based strategies for battery operation are beneficial for both the system operator as well as the storage operator.
the use of LiBs for secondary reserve provision can yield cost savings in the range of 20% to 50%, depending on the market design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a model-based dispatch strategy can be used to increase the value of storage systems by reducing the costs of reserve provision.
model-based dispatch strategies can significantly reduce LiB operation costs.
a simple model-based dispatch strategy is able to outperform an ad-hoc strategy that maximizes the utilization of LiB in a secondary reserve market.
